title: Writing the High Society arrangement and Armstrong's ending
summary: Randolph wrote the arrangement, using the New Orleans clarinet chorus for saxophones and chords mirrored above the harmony, and also wrote Armstrong's ending.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you have any of that feeling -- a sense of history while you were doing it? I wouldn't imagine
so - - that what you were recording, what you were playing was going to be --
No. Just really didn't. And I'll tell you another thing I did for Louie, one of the many things I did for him was -- da-da-da- -- High Society.
Yes. I was playing that record today and I noticed that you played the lead at one part.
Yes, I did.
And the saxes are playing the traditional clarinet solo. De-de-de-de- --
Yes. De-de-de-de-
You wrote that arrangement?
I wrote that arrangement, yeah.
Where did you learn that clarinet chorus? Because before then it had not been recorded with the traditional --
No, it certainly hadn't
Where did you learn it?

I learned it from --let's see, who did I get that from? Da-da-da-da--- Well, that's the part I used -- Well, I used -- I didn't use all of it, because I just used just that much. That's all I could think of. I think I heard some of the boys in the band doing it. One of the clarinet players, either Al Washington -- Al Washington, I think, I heard doing that. Either Al did or Preston must have sang it to
It's a New Orleans thing.

Yes, a New Orleans -- yeah, because they told me -- especially Bessie told me, she said, "That's High Society," don't do it without that." That's when I mirrored the chord. You know how I went out -- do-do-do-do -- went above the chords, you know?
Yes, yes.
Went above the thing. And had Louie-da-da-da -- one of those things.
Would you suggest how Louie should build the ending, say, or did --
No, I would just write it -- I'd just write it and Louie'd make it just like I had it in mind.
Oh, you wrote the ending?
Yes, I wrote --
You wrote the things that Louie was to play?
Yeah, oh, yes. I really would, and Louie'd play it.
I didn't know that. I don't think that's ever been revealed before.
Yes, I would write that thing, Louie would play it just like that.
